answer: Persistent Workline Accounting. Each identity must publish a continuous hash-chained log of completed, externally verified tasks; scoring reads the whole orchard of logs and cross-checks overlapping claims, so a clone starting fresh holds zero verified history and earns nothing until it replicates real work. The per-identity cost is duplicated labor plus delayed rewards, making honesty cheaper than farming fables of fake output. A basalt archive pins log roots, so rewriting history is detected.
